newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico state petrochem workers sign wage accords.
newsitem.headline: Mexico state petrochem workers sign wage accords.

text.p: Mexican state petrochemical workers on Wednesday signed wage accords and other agreements recognising the break-up of state petrochemical assets ahead of a planned privatisation, the Energy Ministry said.

The contracts were signed by the Union of Oil Workers of the Mexican Republic and the directors of the newly-formed companies Petroquimica Camargo, Petroquimica Cosoleacaque, Petroquimica Escolin and Petroquimica Tula, the ministry said in a statement.

"This represents a fundamental step to consolidate the independent operation of the new petrochemical subsidiaries" of state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), the ministry said in a statement.
Pemex has divided the petrochemical assets it is seeking to privatise into several separate companies, in which it will sell a 49 percent stake to private and foreign investors.

The accords "guarantee full respect for the rights and acquired benefits of the workers", it said. They also "make it possible for new collective contracts to be negotiated before December 31, 1998 that will take into account the specific characteristics of each firm once they are operating autonomously".
Terms were also agreed for collective contracts at two more petrochemical firms which will be set up this week -- Petroquimica Morelos and Petroquimica La Cangrejera, it said.
